title: UCLIR: Unsupervised Continual Learning using Independent Representations
abstract: arXiv:2611.24093v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In continual learning, regularization-based methods aim to mimic neuroplasticity by updating network weights to learn new tasks while constraining changes to parameters that are important for previously learned tasks through penalty terms. However, as the number of tasks increases, preserving knowledge from earlier tasks becomes less effective. This is mainly because updates for new tasks are distributed across the entire network, where parameters are highly interdependent due to the dense connectivity between neurons. Inspired by the Exponential Distance Rule (EDR), which states that the number of neural connections decreases with increasing physical distance, learning is naturally locally correlated while inter-area updates remain less task-dependent. translated_title: UCLIR：基于独立表示的无监督持续学习
translated_abstract: 在持续学习中，基于正则化的方法旨在通过更新网络权重来学习新任务，同时通过惩罚项约束对先前学习任务重要的参数的变化，从而模拟神经可塑性。然而，随着任务数量的增加，对早期任务知识的保护效果会逐渐减弱。这主要是因为新任务的更新分布在整个网络中，而由于神经元之间密集的连接，参数高度相互依赖。受指数距离规则的启发——该规则指出神经连接的数量随物理距离的增加而减少——学习在本质上具有局部相关性，而区域间的更新则较少依赖于特定任务。基于这一原理，本文证明了对多个小型且独立学习的互补表示应用权重正则化是更为有效的……
tldr: 该论文提出UCLIR方法，受大脑指数距离规则启发，通过对多个独立学习的小型互补表示分别施加权重正则化，有效解决了持续学习中随任务增加旧知识保留效果下降的问题。
en_tdlr: Inspired by the Exponential Distance Rule, this paper proposes UCLIR, demonstrating that applying weight regularization to multiple small, independently learned complementary representations is more effective for preserving knowledge of earlier tasks in continual learning.
